newsitem.title: USA: More moderate earthquakes shake Pacific Northwest.
newsitem.headline: More moderate earthquakes shake Pacific Northwest.

text.p: A series of moderate earthquakes shook the Pacific Northwest region of the United States on Tuesday, following a slightly stronger tremor the day before.
No injuries or damage were reported from any of the quakes, according to the U.S. Geological Survey.

Three tremors ranging in intensity from 3.0 to 4.2 on the Richter scale were reported during an 18-minute period on Tuesday morning, survey spokesman John Minsch said. Two of them rattled an area 140 miles (225 km) northeast of Seattle and the third hit 170 miles (275 km) north of Seattle.
They followed a quake of 4.9 on the Richter scale centred 15 miles (25 km) west of Seattle on Monday. That was the most intense tremor in the region since May 1996.
But Tuesday's tremors were independent events and not related to Monday's tremor, according to earthquake experts at the Geological Survey and the University of Washington.
There was no evidence to suggest the series of tremors represented a precursor to a major earthquake, the experts added, calling the timing of the seismic activity a coincidence.
